title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #981 asks for the asymptotic behavior of ∑_{p<x} f_ε(p) where f_ε(p) is the stabilization threshold for character sums. Elliott (1969) proved ∑_{p<x} f_ε(p) ~ c_ε · x/log x. Tang-Zhang (2025) studied an alternative first-passage formulation.
mathContext: The problem connects character sums (Legendre symbol), quadratic residues, and prime distribution.

title: Core Definitions: Legendre Symbol and Stabilization
content: legendreInt n p: Legendre symbol (n/p) as integer (+1, -1, or 0). characterSum N p: partial sum ∑_{n<N} (n/p). isBoundedFrom ε p m: |characterSum N p| < εN for all N ≥ m. fEps ε p: smallest m satisfying the bound (stabilization threshold). These definitions formalize when character sum cancellation becomes permanently effective.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of core definitions: legendre symbol and stabilization

title: Sum Over Primes and Asymptotic Function
content: sumFEps ε x (axiom): ∑_{p<x} f_ε(p), the sum of stabilization thresholds over primes less than x. Axiomatized because constructing Fact instances from Finset membership requires complex dependent types. asymptoticFunc x = x/log x: the Prime Number Theorem form that appears in the asymptotic.
mathContext: Axiomatizing sumFEps avoids sorry in the original definition while preserving the mathematical content.

title: Elliott's Theorem (1969)
content: elliott_1969: For any ε > 0, ∃ c_ε > 0 such that sumFEps(ε,x)/asymptoticFunc(x) → c_ε. This is the main result resolving Erdős's conjecture. elliott_1969_quantitative: the ε-δ form — for any δ > 0, eventually the ratio is within δ of c_ε.
mathContext: Elliott's 1969 paper in Indag. Math. completely resolved the conjecture using deep analytic techniques.

title: Character Sum Bounds and Properties
content: polya_vinogradov: |characterSum N p| ≤ √p · log p (classical 1918 bound). character_sum_cancellation: eventually |characterSum N p| ≤ √N · log N (square-root cancellation). fEps_finite: f_ε(p) is well-defined for all primes. burgess_bound: improved bounds for short character sums (1962). These results provide the theoretical foundation for Elliott's asymptotic.
mathContext: The Pólya-Vinogradov inequality guarantees f_ε(p) is finite; Burgess gives sharper estimates for subintervals.

title: Quadratic Residues and Complete Sums
content: isQuadraticResidue a p: ∃ x, x² ≡ a (mod p). Exactly (p-1)/2 residues and (p-1)/2 non-residues exist among nonzero classes mod p. complete_sum_zero: ∑_{n=0}^{p-1} (n/p) = 0, since QRs and NQRs cancel perfectly over a full period. This periodicity constrains the growth of partial character sums.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of quadratic residues and complete sums

title: Alternative Formulation (Tang-Zhang 2025)
content: fEpsAlt ε p: smallest m with |characterSum m p| < εm (first-passage time, not eventual-time). sumFEpsAlt ε x (axiom): sum of fEpsAlt over primes < x. tang_zhang_2025: ∃ c' > 0 with sumFEpsAlt(ε,x)/asymptoticFunc(x) → c'. Both formulations give PNT-form asymptotics but with potentially different constants.
mathContext: First-passage (when does it first become small?) vs eventual-time (when does it stay small?) give different thresholds.

title: Complete Resolution
content: erdos_981 (main theorem): combines Elliott's asymptotic and Tang-Zhang's alternative into a conjunction. Proved by exact ⟨elliott_1969 ε hε, tang_zhang_2025 ε hε⟩. Both the original stabilization and the first-passage formulation have PNT-form asymptotics ∑_{p<x} f(p) ~ c · x/log x.
